instructions: Drain the crab well. In a small bowl, gently stir together the crab, the softened cream cheese, the sliced green onion, 1 tsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp soy sauce and the garlic powder. Stir just until combined so the crab stays in flakes.

Pour the oil into a medium heavy pot so it's about 1 inch deep. Heat it over medium to 325°F. If you don't have a thermometer, drop in a scrap of wonton wrapper. It should sizzle gently and turn golden in about 30 seconds.
While the oil heats, set out a small bowl of water. Work with 3 wrappers at a time and keep the rest covered. Spoon 2 tsp of filling into the center of each wrapper.

Wet the edges of each wrapper with a finger dipped in the water. Fold two opposite corners together to make a triangle and press the edges to seal. Dampen the two tips and fold them in. Repeat until the filling is used up.
Fry 6 at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're deep golden and crisp. Turn them once if one side is browning faster. Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels.
Let the oil come back to 325°F between batches. Serve warm.
method_notes: The lead is Spend With Pennies (4.89 from 409): canned crab, cream cheese, green onion, Worcestershire, soy, garlic powder, 2 tsp filling per wrapper, fried at 325°F for 2 to 3 minutes. Dinner at the Zoo could not be read (blocked), so there was no second source to compare. The lead also gives baking (425°F, 12 to 14 minutes) and air frying; this version fries, since that is the crisp one. Sweet and sour dip is left out because the lead doesn't include one.
